learn-core-skills.title: Nuclear Critical Core Skills
learn-core-skills.purpose: The 16 human and thinking skills every role at a nuclear plant needs, how each maps to international frameworks, and how each is developed and assessed.

learn-core-skill.title: Core skill
learn-core-skill.purpose: One core skill: what it looks like at the plant, its levels, benchmark mappings, development and assessment routes, and family targets.

my-core-skills.title: My core skills
my-core-skills.purpose: Your evidence for each core skill against your family's target, why, and the next step.

my-core-practice.title: Situational judgement practice
my-core-practice.purpose: Practise plant scenarios for the core skills and see the expert's reasoning. For development only.

workforce-core-skills.title: Core skills across ENEC
workforce-core-skills.purpose: Evidence against targets and practice participation by core skill, cluster and family, suppressed under 10.

training-sjt-items.title: Situational judgement item bank
training-sjt-items.purpose: The practice scenarios, expert ratings and rationales in English and Arabic; the training manager maintains them.

my-problem-solving.title: Adaptive problem-solving practice
my-problem-solving.purpose: Work through plant scenarios where the information changes mid-task, see the expert's reasoning at every stage and track yourself on a defined practice scale. For development only.

training-aps-scenarios.title: Problem-solving scenario bank
training-aps-scenarios.purpose: The staged scenarios behind adaptive problem-solving practice, each with at least one mid-task change, in English and Arabic.

learn-role-play.title: Role-play practice library
learn-role-play.purpose: ENEC-authored conversations to practise, from pre-job briefs to coaching a peer on AI output, each with its published rubric in English and Arabic.

my-role-play.title: My role-play practice
my-role-play.purpose: Practise conversations, keep your feedback history privately and ask a reviewer to validate a session as evidence.

my-role-play-scenario.title: Role-play session
my-role-play-scenario.purpose: Answer the counterpart turn by turn and see which rubric criteria each answer meets. What you type is never stored.

training-role-play.title: Role-play reviews and library
training-role-play.purpose: Validate the role-play sessions sent to you as evidence, or decline with a reason; maintain the role-play library.

workforce-core-practice.title: Practice participation
workforce-core-practice.purpose: Problem-solving and role-play practice in aggregate only, suppressed under 10 people.

clusterSub.thinking_critically: Questioning, deciding conservatively, using procedures, seeing the whole system and solving problems at their cause.
clusterSub.interacting_with_others: Checking each other, communicating under pressure, speaking up, working across cultures and developing others.
clusterSub.staying_relevant: Learning fast, managing yourself, adapting to change, using digital tools with judgement and owning your work.

need.aria: Level {level} of 3 against a target of {target}

reason.none: No evidence yet on the {n} catalogue skills linked to this core skill.
reason.met: Core level {level} meets your family target of {target}.
reason.below: Core level {level} is below your family target of {target}.
reason.noTarget: Core level {level}; your role has no family target for this skill.
reason.practice: Practice: {pct}% of the expert's best across {n} scenarios. Shown for development; it does not change the level.

fw.intro: Sixteen human and thinking skills every role at a nuclear plant needs, in the three SkillsFuture clusters. Each is written for the plant, mapped to at least two international frameworks and kept only because it has its own development and assessment approach.

cta.signIn: Sign in to see your core skills
cta.body: Staff see their own evidence for each core skill against their family target, and can practise plant scenarios with the expert's reasoning.

matrix.title: Mapping matrix
matrix.intro: Which frameworks each core skill maps to. Every benchmark is a sourced row in the registry; open a chip for the source and as-of date.

rule.title: The inclusion rule
rule.intro: Following McKinsey's DELTA research, a core skill exists only if it needs its own way to develop it and its own way to assess it. The rule runs on the definitions below every time this page loads.
rule.r1: A development route of its own, beyond generic practice.
rule.r2: An assessment route of its own, beyond generic practice.
rule.r3: No two skills share the same development and assessment approach.
rule.r4: At least two benchmark mappings, and no wellbeing competency.

problem.no_development: no development route of its own
problem.no_assessment: no assessment route of its own
problem.shared_approach: shares its approach with another skill
problem.wellbeing: a wellbeing competency is not allowed
problem.count: the set should hold 16 core skills

wellbeing.title: Wellbeing is an outcome, not a skill
wellbeing.body: SkillsFuture's 2025 review found wellbeing and career health are best treated as outcomes within existing skills. Kafa'a follows it: there is no wellbeing competency and no wellbeing score; Resilience and self-management and Learning agility carry them as outcomes, and no health information is recorded.

cs.notFound: This core skill was not found.
cs.atPlant: What it looks like at the plant
cs.levelsNote: Three levels, 1 to {max}. A catalogue skill held at level 3 or above counts as Role model.
cs.routes: How it is developed and assessed
cs.routesIntro: Each core skill has its own route for both. That is why it is a core skill (the inclusion rule).
cs.outcome: An outcome, not a separate skill
cs.targetsIntro: The level each family needs, with the reason.
cs.tryBody: Practise plant scenarios for this skill and compare your choice with the expert's. Development only; nothing is gated.

my.intro: Your evidence for each Nuclear Critical Core Skill, from the skill states in your passport, against your job family's target. Practice results sit beside it for your development only.
my.none: Core skills are shown to ENEC staff with a skills passport.

tile.belowSub: a development route is listed for each

my.practiceTitle: Your practice score on this skill's scenarios in the last four quarters (development only)

how.title: How your level is worked out
how.body: Each core skill links to catalogue skills. Your level is your highest evidenced level on those skills (3 or above counts as Role model), the same rule on the server and in this page. Open "Why this?" for the evidence behind each one.

private.title: Practice stays yours
private.body: Your situational judgement practice is visible only to you. It never changes your level, never gates a qualification and never appears in talent review.

sjt.intro: Short plant scenarios for the core skills. Choose what you would do, then see how the expert rates every response and why. For your development only.
sjt.none: Practice is for ENEC staff with a skills passport.

q.noKey: The expert's ratings appear after you answer.

verdict.0: The expert sees this response as counterproductive

effSub.1: Well meant but leaves the risk.
effSub.2: Safe, but not the strongest response.
effSub.3: What an experienced professional would do.

fb.rationale: Why the expert answers this way

sjt.doneBody: You worked through {n} scenarios. Your result is below and stays with you.

start.title: Start a practice set
start.b1: Up to 8 plant scenarios, mixed or for one core skill.
start.b2: After each answer you see the expert's rating of every response and the reasoning.
start.b3: Scenarios you have seen least come first.
start.b4: For development only: no pass mark, nothing gated, no points or streaks.

scale.title: How responses are rated
scale.note: Your score is the share of the expert's best, where every best response counts {max}.

sjt.noResultBody: Start a set to see your result and trend here.

res.title: Latest result ({period})
res.intro: Your score with the ENEC average as a reference line, and the skills you were strongest and weakest on.
res.enecSuppressed: The ENEC average is shown when at least 10 people have practised.
res.meaning: This is practice, not an assessment. Use it to see where your judgement differs from the expert's, then read the rationale.

trend.title: My trend
trend.one: Your trend appears after practice in two quarters.

private.title: Development only
private.body: Your practice is visible only to you. It never writes skill evidence, never gates a qualification, never reaches your manager or talent review, and HR sees only aggregates of 10 or more people.

reason.score: {score}% of the expert's best across {n} scenarios; you chose the expert's best response {best} times.
reason.develop: To develop: {skill} ({pct}%). Read the rationales and try a focused set.
reason.private: This result is yours only and is never used in talent review.

wf.intro: The core skills across ENEC: evidence against family targets, and situational judgement practice. Aggregates only; any cell under 10 people is suppressed.
wf.none: This view is for HR (aggregate access).

tile.metSub: share of person x skill pairs

wf.byFamilyEyebrow: families of 10 or more; security, safeguards and cyber are never broken out

sjt.devBody: Practice results are never shown per person, never gate anything and never feed talent review.

def.title: Definitions
def.d1: A target is met when a person's core level (their highest evidenced level on the linked catalogue skills, capped at 3) reaches their job family's target.
def.d2: Practice score: the share of the expert's best across the scenarios answered (each best response counts 3).
def.d3: Cells naming fewer than 10 people show as suppressed (<10).
def.d4: Security, safeguards and cyber families are never broken out.

bank.intro: The situational judgement scenarios behind the practice, with the expert's rating and reasoning for every response, in English and Arabic.

coverage.title: Active scenarios per core skill
coverage.ok: Every core skill has enough scenarios ({n} active).

rules.title: Item rules
rules.eyebrow: checked by the server on every save
rules.r1: The scenario, four responses, a why for each and the expert rationale, all in English and Arabic.
rules.r2: Every response rated 0 to 3, with exactly one expert's best response.
rules.r3: Each core skill keeps at least two active scenarios.
rules.r4: Nothing about plant security; no exam content.
rules.r5: Every save is versioned and audited.

bank.readonly: You can read the bank; only the training manager edits it.

security.title: Practice, not security
security.body: Scenarios never describe security arrangements or exam content. The server refuses restricted wording.

problem.stem: Write the scenario in English and Arabic.
problem.options: Write all four responses in both languages.
problem.key: Rate every response 0-3 with exactly one expert's best.
problem.notes: Write a why for every response in both languages.
problem.rationale: Write the expert rationale in English and Arabic.

bank.retireBody: It stops appearing in new practice sets. Past results keep it. Each core skill must keep two active scenarios.

edit.help: Every text in English and Arabic. The same rules the server applies are checked as you type; the save is checked again and audited.
edit.json: The scenario must be valid JSON (one object).

aps.intro: Plant scenarios that change while you work: you set a plan, then a schedule slips, readings disagree or a part is late. At each stage you judge which facts matter and choose what to do, then see the expert's rating and reasoning. For development only.
aps.none: No problem-solving practice is available for your profile.

how.title: Plan, notice, adapt
how.s1: Read the situation and set your first plan.
how.s2: New information arrives only after you commit: decide whether it changes your plan.
how.s3: Where facts are listed, tick the ones that matter for your decision.
how.s4: After each answer you see every option's rating, why, and the expert's debrief.

aps.doneBody: Your result is below. It stays private to you and is never used for a qualification.

cat.title: Scenarios
cat.intro: Each scenario has at least one mid-task change. Pick any; the suggestion is the one you have practised least.

aps.cuesEyebrow: Tick every fact that should shape your decision
aps.noKey: The expert's key appears after you answer.

verdict.0: That choice would make things worse
verdict.held: You kept the old plan although the change called for a new one
verdict.overreact: You changed course although the best move was to keep the plan

bandSub.emerging: Plans often miss the facts that matter, and changes are not yet picked up.
bandSub.developing: Sound first plans; changes are noticed but not always acted on well.
bandSub.adaptive: Notices what matters and revises the plan when the facts call for it.
bandSub.strategic: Consistently sets strong plans, separates signal from noise and adapts without overreacting.

dim.adapt: Revising the plan when things change

scale.title: The practice scale
scale.note: Kafa'a's own scale, 0 to 100: the share of the most points you could reach across every stage. Each choice earns its expert rating (0-3) twice over; each fact judged correctly earns one point. Four bands with fixed cut points. It measures practice on these scenarios only.
scale.piaacNote: Shown as context only: PIAAC is a different test on a different scale. Your practice score is never converted to it.

aps.noResultBody: Complete a scenario to see your score on the practice scale with the ENEC comparison.

res.title: My latest result ({period})
res.intro: Your score with the scale definition, the ENEC average and the PIAAC line as context.
res.line: My score on the practice scale
res.enecSuppressed: The ENEC average shows once 10 or more people have practised.
res.dimsNote: Plan counts the first stage, adapt the change stages and notice the facts you judged.

trend.title: My trend
trend.one: Practise in more than one quarter to see a trend.

hist.title: My runs
hist.never: Never a qualification gate, never skill evidence

private.title: Private to you
private.body: Your runs are visible to you only. HR sees practice participation in aggregate, suppressed under 10 people; managers see nothing.

gate.title: Never a gate
gate.body: Practice results never decide a qualification, an authorisation or a talent review, and they are not skill evidence.

reason.changes: You handled {ok} of {n} mid-task changes well.
reason.held: At least once you kept the old plan when the change called for a new one.
reason.overreact: At least once you changed course when keeping the plan was best.
reason.private: Private practice: never a qualification gate or skill evidence.
reason.next: {theme}: you have practised this scenario {n} times, the least of the bank.

problem.text: Title, summary and context are needed in English and Arabic.
problem.core_skill: Link one to three core skills.
problem.skills: Link one to four catalogue skills.
problem.stages: A scenario has two to four stages.
problem.first_stage: The first stage sets the plan (stage ids a-z, 0-9, -).
problem.no_change: Every later stage is a mid-task change, and there is at least one.
problem.stage_text: Every stage needs its situation, question and debrief in English and Arabic.
problem.options: Three or four options, each with a why in both languages.
problem.key: Rate every option 0-3 with exactly one best (3).
problem.keep: Only a change stage may mark one option as keeping the plan.
problem.cues: Facts to judge: none, or three to five with at least one that matters and one that does not.
problem.status: Status is draft, published or retired.

bank.intro: The staged scenarios behind adaptive problem-solving practice: every option's rating and why, which facts matter and the expert debrief, in English and Arabic. Every scenario carries at least one mid-task change.
bank.allChange: {n} of {total} scenarios carry a mid-task change (the database refuses one without).

rules.title: Rules every scenario meets
rules.r1: Two to four stages: the plan, then at least one mid-task change revealed only after the previous answer.
rules.r2: Three or four options per stage, rated 0-3 with exactly one best, each with a why in both languages.
rules.r3: Optional facts to judge (three to five), at least one that matters and one that does not.
rules.r4: A change stage may make keeping the plan the best move, so overreacting is scored too.
rules.r5: No plant-security, safeguards or cyber detail; every save is audited.

bank.caption: Problem-solving scenarios
bank.security: Scenarios use realistic but generic plant situations. They never describe security arrangements, safeguards or cyber configuration.
bank.publishedBody: Staff can practise this scenario once it is published. The server re-checks every rule first.
bank.retiredBody: Staff can no longer start this scenario. Past runs keep their scores; at least three scenarios stay published.

kind.raise_concern: Raising a concern to a senior
kind.ai_peer_coaching: Coaching a peer on AI output

check.question: Asks at least one question.
check.digit: Gives at least one number (a time, value or count).

rp.sources: Built on {n} sources (see the research packs).
rp.notStoredLong: Only which criteria each answer met and its word count are kept. What you typed was never stored.
rp.withdrawBody: {name} will no longer see this session. You can ask again later.

speak.title: Is this a real concern?
speak.body: Role-play is practice. A real concern about safety, conduct or wrongdoing belongs in the speak-up channels, which protect you.
speak.routed: What you wrote reads like a real concern, so it was not sent or stored as practice. Please use the speak-up channels.

lib.intro: Conversations nuclear professionals have to get right, written by ENEC. Each shows its published rubric, in English and Arabic, so you know exactly what the check looks for before you practise.

how.title: Practise the conversation, see the rubric
how.s1: Read the setting, who you are talking to and your role.
how.s2: Answer each turn in your own words, in English or Arabic.
how.s3: The published rubric ticks each criterion; the example answer shows one good way.
how.s4: Your feedback is private. At the mark, you may ask a named reviewer to validate it as evidence.

lib.listIntro: Every published scenario with its rubric.

private.title: Your practice stays private
private.body: Sessions and feedback are visible to you only. A reviewer sees a session only when you send it to them by name.

mine.intro: Your role-play practice. Feedback is saved privately; nobody else sees it unless you ask a reviewer to validate a session.
mine.privateBody: Line managers, HR, instructors, auditors and administrators cannot read your role-play history. A reviewer you name sees only the session you send, with its ticks and your context, never your words.

ask.title: Ask a reviewer to validate this session
ask.body: Once validated, this session becomes rating evidence (basis validated) on the scenario's skills. The reviewer sees the ticks, the rubric and your context, never your answers.
ask.noReviewers: No reviewer is available right now.
ask.contextHint: 5 to 400 characters, for example where you will use this conversation. No contact details.

session.intro: Answer the counterpart turn by turn. Each answer is checked against the published rubric; only the ticks are kept.
session.b1: Answer as you would at work, in English or Arabic.
session.b2: After each answer you see which criteria it met and an example answer.
session.b3: Nothing you type is stored; real concerns go to the speak-up channels.
session.privateBody: Only you see this session and its feedback.
session.doneBody: Your feedback is saved privately in your history.

tr.intro: Sessions sent to you for validation, with the ticks, the rubric and the person's context (never their answers), and the role-play library.
tr.noQueue: Reviews are for instructors, the training manager and the HR authority.
tr.ruleBody: You see only sessions sent to you by name. Validating writes rating evidence (basis validated) on the scenario's skills and recomputes them; declining needs a reason. You can never decide your own session.
tr.emptyBody: Sessions people send you by name appear here.
tr.validateBody: This writes validated rating evidence for {person} at level {level} on: {list}. It is practice feedback, not a qualification. The person is notified.
tr.declineBody: No evidence is written. The person sees your reason.
tr.libWrite: You maintain the library: add, edit, publish or retire scenarios. Every save is checked and audited.
tr.libRead: Read-only: the training manager maintains the library.
tr.publishedBody: Staff can practise this scenario and read its rubric once published. The server re-checks every rule first.
tr.retiredBody: Staff can no longer start this scenario. Saved feedback stays in each person's history; at least three scenarios stay published.
tr.security: Scenarios and answers never touch plant security, safeguards or cyber details; such wording is refused.

reason.ready: At or above the scenario's mark of {mark}%: you can ask a reviewer to validate it.
reason.notReady: Below the scenario's mark of {mark}%: practise again before asking for validation.
reason.private: Saved privately: visible to you only.

problem.text: Title, summary, setting, counterpart and your role are needed in English and Arabic.
problem.core_skill: Link one to three core skills.
problem.skills: Link one to four catalogue skills that can carry evidence.
problem.rubric: Three to eight criteria with distinct ids.
problem.criterion: Every criterion needs a label, what it looks for and a tip in English and Arabic.
problem.check: Every criterion needs a valid check (cue words, length, a question or a number).
problem.turns: Three to five turns with distinct ids.
problem.turn: Every turn needs the counterpart's line, a hint and an example answer in English and Arabic.
problem.turn_criteria: Every turn checks one to five known criteria.
problem.unused: Every criterion is checked by at least one turn.
problem.status: Status is draft, published or retired.

wp.intro: Problem-solving and role-play practice in aggregate. Any figure naming fewer than 10 people is suppressed and no person is listed.
wp.none: No practice figures are available for your access.

aps.title: Adaptive problem-solving practice
aps.intro: Latest completed run per person in the last four quarters.

rp.title: Role-play practice
rp.intro: Completed sessions in the last four quarters; the rate pools every criterion checked.

wp.privacyBody: Nobody's runs, sessions or feedback are shown here. Cells under 10 people show as suppressed.
wp.gateBody: These figures inform training design. They never gate a qualification and are never used in talent review.
